Architecture Diagram

The solution contains one server-rendered catalog web application with a selectable mock-data mode or an Entity Framework-backed SQL Server mode. Catalog pages call an in-process service; no separately deployed application services are defined in this solution.

Data Storage & External Services

When mock data is disabled, Entity Framework connects to SQL Server LocalDB using the CatalogDBContext connection string. With the checked-in UseMockData=true setting, the application instead uses a shared in-memory catalog list. Application Insights is configured for request, dependency, and exception telemetry; no remote business-service integration or message broker is configured.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • The application uses Web Forms page handlers and an ICatalogService abstraction rather than a REST API.
  • Autofac selects either the in-memory mock service or the Entity Framework service from UseMockData.
  • Entity Framework maps catalog items to required catalog-brand and catalog-type relationships.

DTOs & Contracts

There are no dedicated API request or response DTOs because the application does not expose a JSON API. CatalogItem, CatalogBrand, and CatalogType are service-level domain entities; PaginatedItemsViewModel is the presentation model returned for browsing. The classes are mutable C# classes, not immutable records. Newtonsoft.Json is declared as a package, but no API serialization contract or OpenAPI specification is present.

Communication Patterns

Web Forms handlers synchronously call ICatalogService; the active implementation is selected through Autofac using UseMockData. CatalogService uses EF6 against LocalDB, while CatalogServiceMock reads and mutates an in-memory list. There are no inter-service HTTP clients, message queues, retry/circuit-breaker policies, API gateway, or service discovery mechanisms. The application contains no explicit API authentication, authorization, or TLS configuration; deployment-level IIS settings are not included in the project configuration.

Core Business Workflows

The application supports browsing and maintaining a product catalog: users can view paginated products, inspect details, and create, update, or delete catalog entries. Product categories and brands provide the catalog's classification data.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalogA product offered in the catalog, with price and inventory informationBelongs to one catalog brand and one catalog type
CatalogBrandCatalogBrand classification for catalog itemsCan be associated with multiple catalog items
CatalogTypeCatalogType/category classification for catalog itemsCan be associated with multiple catalog items

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
eShopLegacyWebForms / CatalogServiceCatalogCatalogItem, CatalogBrand, CatalogTypeEF6 and SQL Server LocalDB when database mode is selected
CatalogServiceMockCatalog mockIn-memory CatalogItem list; preconfigured brands and typesNone

This is a single application and bounded context. There are no cross-domain services or remote data-exchange patterns.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse the catalog

  1. A visitor opens the catalog or requests a page using the index and size route values.
  2. The page uses defaults of page size 10 and index 0 unless route values are supplied.
  3. ICatalogService.GetCatalogItemsPaginated obtains a page; the EF implementation includes brand and type data, while mock mode uses its shared list.
  4. The page renders product data and previous/next navigation.

Workflow 2: Create or update a catalog item

  1. A catalog editor opens the create or edit page and enters product values.
  2. The page checks ModelState.IsValid; the model defines price format/range and inventory-range constraints.
  3. On create, the service assigns an identifier, adds the item, and saves it; mock mode assigns an in-memory identifier.
  4. On update, the service marks the item modified and saves it.
  5. Successful operations redirect to the catalog; invalid model state leaves the user on the form.

Workflow 3: Delete a catalog item

  1. An editor opens the delete page for an item and reviews its details.
  2. The delete postback identifies the item and calls ICatalogService.RemoveCatalogItem.
  3. The active service removes it from the database or mock collection, then the page redirects to the catalog.

Cross-Service Data Flows

No cross-service composition occurs. The page layer gets catalog data from one in-process catalog service; the production implementation retrieves it from EF6, and the mock implementation reads the in-memory collection. The database initializer can seed preconfigured records or application-local customization files.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Editor as "Catalog Editor" participant Page as "Create Catalog Page" participant Service as "Catalog Service" participant Generator as "HiLo ID Generator" participant DB as "SQL Server LocalDB" Editor->>Page: Submit new product details Page->>Page: Check model validation alt Values are valid Page->>Service: Create catalog item Service->>Generator: Request item identifier Generator->>DB: Read next sequence when current range is exhausted DB-->>Generator: Sequence value Generator-->>Service: Assign identifier Service->>DB: Save catalog item with EF6 DB-->>Service: Save succeeds Service-->>Page: Operation completed Page-->>Editor: Redirect to catalog else Validation fails Page-->>Editor: Show form with validation errors end

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • Catalog items require a type and brand in the EF model.
  • Price is constrained to non-negative values with at most two decimal places; stock, restock, and maximum-stock values have a 0 to 10,000,000 range.
  • Catalog item identifiers come from the SQL sequence/hi-lo generator in database mode and from the current maximum ID in mock mode.
  • UseMockData selects whether catalog changes persist to EF/LocalDB or to the process-local mock list.
  • Create and edit page handlers only save when ModelState.IsValid; the service methods perform create/update/delete persistence and do not implement a separate approval or state-transition process.
  • Page actions do not show explicit business-role or resource-ownership checks; deployment authentication and authorization are not established by these application files.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The project targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and uses legacy Web Forms, EF6, and older ASP.NET packages. The declared Newtonsoft.Json 12.0.1 package is affected by CVE-2024-21907; the first patched version is 13.0.1. A direct dotnet list package --include-transitive inventory could not complete because the legacy project imports a missing Visual Studio WebApplication target, so the count and versions here are from packages.config.

Notable Observations

  • The package set includes several separate Application Insights modules at version 2.9.1, plus the 2.4.0 agent intercept package.
  • The project also declares browser libraries through NuGet (Bootstrap, jQuery, Popper.js, Modernizr, and Respond).
  • Microsoft.Net.Compilers is marked developmentDependency=true; it is compiler tooling rather than an application runtime library.
  • No package is declared with a test scope, and no test dependencies were detected.

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

The catalog model contains three EF6 entities stored in SQL Server LocalDB when database mode is selected. An in-memory mock service is also registered by default in the checked-in application settings.

Entity Model

CatalogItem is defined in src/eShopLegacyWebForms/Models/CatalogItem.cs; CatalogBrand and CatalogType are in their correspondingly named files. The EF mapping makes each item's brand and type required. PictureUri is not persisted. The catalog item identifier is generated using a SQL sequence and the hi-lo generator.

Caching Strategy

No cache provider, cache annotations, or explicit cache policy is configured. The mock implementation keeps catalog data in a process-wide in-memory list because it is registered as a singleton in mock mode; this is the data source, not a read-through cache. Database mode reads through EF6.

Data Ownership Boundaries

The application is a single catalog bounded context with one database and no cross-service database access. CatalogService is the database-facing owner of catalog operations; the page handlers call its interface rather than querying EF directly. Mock mode replaces persistence with an in-process collection. There is no CQRS or cross-service aggregation.
